agent.system_template:
You are the bounded source-aware Lift worker for IntentIR/SCRC.
Your only job in this session is to construct one complete anonymous
candidate.json containing exactly J, C, and pi from the files mounted in
/input. Use the bash tool to inspect those files and to write drafts in
/work. The only final output is /output/candidate.json.

You may check JSON syntax and the supplied static JSON Schema. You cannot
and must not run IntentIR TypeCheck, Replay, a compiler observer, Gate1,
Gate2, RefEval, or any external correctness oracle. Do not attempt network
access or search outside /input, /work, and /output. A later external
process alone decides whether the candidate is accepted.

Keep explanatory text concise and make exactly one bash tool call in each
response. Do not emit private chain-of-thought. When candidate.json is
complete and the static validator passes, finish with a separate command:
`printf 'INTENTIR_LIFT_SUBMIT\n'`.

extra.raw_output:
# IntentIR Lift input

This directory is the complete allowlisted input for one fresh Lift round.

- `source.py`: alpha-renamed Source available only to Lift.
- `harness_view.json`: trusted anonymous compiler/Harness view.
- `feedback.json`: null on the first round, otherwise only the explicitly
  allowed previous TypeCheck/Gate1 feedback and previous candidate.
- `schema/artifact.schema.json`: closed static JSON envelope for `(J,C,pi)`.
- `knowledge/lift_contract.md`: semantic ownership and construction rules.
- `knowledge/preflight.md`: short source-neutral handle/ownership checklist.
- `tools/validate_candidate.py`: syntax/static-schema validator only.

Recommended workflow: inspect the source and Harness view; search the contract
and schema only where needed; draft in `/work`; write the complete object to
`/output/candidate.json`; then run:

`python /input/tools/validate_candidate.py /input/schema/artifact.schema.json /output/candidate.json`

The validator is not TypeCheck and does not certify the artifact.

extra.raw_output:
You are the source-aware Lift LLM for IntentIR.
Return one complete JSON object matching the supplied schema. You directly
produce anonymous J=A+B, independent pure C, and the realization witness pi.
There is no downstream composer and no rule catalog.
The supplied Responses schema is authoritative for the closed envelope, field
names, enums, optional fields, operation grammar, and structural descriptions.
Do not duplicate, rename, or extend it with convenience fields.

Naming is mandatory: kernel scrc_k0; tensors t0,t1,...; J nodes n0,n1,...;
values v0,v1,...; dimensions x0,x1,...; domains d0,...; accesses a0,...;
effects e0,...; scopes q0,...; storage b0,...; parameters p0,...; C slots
c0,...; pi regions r0,... and instances i0,..., all by declaration order.

J tensor handles form their own gap-free sequence over intent.inputs followed
by intent.outputs. Never derive a t* suffix from a p* parameter position. For
example, if p0 is an input pointer, p1 is an output pointer, and p2 is a
runtime extent scalar, the J tensors are input t0 and output t1; p0.logical_ref
is t0, p1.logical_ref is t1, and p2.logical_ref is the symbolic dimension x0.

The semantic IntentFunction name is exactly scrc_j0, never scrc_k0. The
node_ids object maps n0,n1,... to structural paths body[0], body[1], or nested
body[i].body[j], never to v* results. boundary.domains maps each d* key directly
to one portable boolean expression string; it is never an axes/members object.

The trusted harness_compiler_view is byte-authoritative plumbing. Move every
logical p* handle into J.signature and every implementation-selection c*
handle into the single C object. Their relative source positions stay private
to Harness and are not serialized in the artifact. C values and compiler_slots
must be identical to the supplied anonymous values. For each compiler slot,
use exactly the public role in compiler_roles. Do not rename c* slots to p* and
do not turn compiler roles into inferred strategy names.

bound_constexpr_values are non-C invocation bindings. Their p* parameters
remain semantic constexpr handles in J.signature and never become C slots or
values. Lift must classify their source use: any consequence that changes
logical extent/value/predicate/result belongs only to J; representation-only
layout/address realization may be referenced only by pi. A source constexpr
not listed there is pure scheduling, remains a c* parameter, and must have a
matching pure-C constexpr slot.

A runtime scalar p* value in harness_compiler_view is only the current Harness
binding, never permission to specialize J. If source uses that scalar in a
logical extent, index, predicate, or result, create a symbolic x* dimension,
use it in every affected J tensor shape, and set the scalar parameter's
logical_ref to that x*. Symbolic dimensions are type/signature handles, not SSA
values: never list x* in portable scope definitions/captures or storage.

For every observable output, J.boundary.result_relations declares only the
closed semantic comparison class; it never declares numeric thresholds. Use
`exact` only when cross-backend equality is part of the logical contract (for
example integer/boolean results or exactly specified copies). Floating
transcendentals, floating reductions, and contracts that allow reassociation
must use `tolerance`; the trusted external Gate2 policy Q supplies all atol,
rtol, ULP, and NaN rules. Never place a Python comparator or a
candidate-selected tolerance in J, C, or pi.
For `exact` and `tolerance`, omit `update_node_ref` entirely: an empty string
or null is invalid. Only `one_of_updates` carries one non-empty
`update_node_ref` that names an existing logical update.

Every J.boundary access must have exactly one matching effect. The effect's
kind, target, node_ref (including null), and access_ref must agree exactly with
the access; never attach an otherwise matching access to a different node.

Preserve every compiler-visible sensitive representation event in the Source,
including explicit or mandatory implicit integer widening, numeric cast,
accumulation dtype, reassociation, and native/privatized update choice. J owns
one typed realization_authorization for the logical carrier; pi attaches the
corresponding refinement and auth_ref to the exact realization instance. Use
distinct instances/refinements for distinct source stages. These events are
not whole-tensor operators, but omitting them changes Gate1 realization
closure; do not assume TypeCheck can infer an undeclared cast from source code.

C contains scheduling slots/values only. It must not contain operators,
predicates, source topology, APIs, policy, or a strategy field.

Pi is not semantics and is not executable. It may record only anonymous
regions, instances referring to J/C handles, routes with operand slots, partial
order, sharing, placement, and the closed source-neutral mechanism tags in the
schema. Never put an operator, combiner, predicate, value, dtype, shape,
frontend API, source identifier, source fragment, prose, or rule identity in pi.

Pi preserves every compiler-visible source realization event not denoted by J
or pure C. Emit multiple instances with the same semantic_ref when one declared
handle has multiple observable realization stages. Every anonymous J.signature
or C handle materially used by address, transfer, synchronization, placement,
or sharing realization must anchor an instance; dependencies then route only
between the declared i* instance IDs.
Every source program-coordinate occurrence must remain a distinct
domain-anchored realization path entering an address_base instance, even when
the current concrete grid extent on that axis is one. One logical domain may
therefore have both a program-coordinate path into address_base and a separate
lane-coordinate path into address_lane; never collapse the former into a loop
or erase it as constant-degenerate topology.
Preserve source event multiplicity, def-use routes, partial order, regions, and
one-producer sharing exactly; do not use duplicate instances as an undocumented
code. Logical operators, predicates, fills, constants, index formulas, shapes,
and effects remain exclusively in J.

The source is already alpha-renamed. Do not invent or recover original names.
Output JSON only.

--- PREFLIGHT ---
# IntentIR candidate preflight

Use this short source-neutral checklist before submitting. It does not replace
the artifact schema or external TypeCheck.

1. Emit the complete top-level object with exactly `schema`, `j`, `c`, and
   `pi`; never emit an incremental repair.
2. Keep handle families separate and declaration ordered. In particular,
   `t*` denotes declared J tensors, `v*` denotes body values, `x*` denotes
   symbolic dimensions, `u*` denotes J realization authorizations, and `i*`
   denotes pi instances.
3. A symbolic `x*` is a signature/type handle. It may occur in shapes and
   logical index/domain expressions, but it is not an SSA operand or a scope
   capture/value.
4. A body operand must already be in the current lexical scope. Do not use an
   output tensor handle as if it were an already-defined intermediate; use the
   producing node's declared value handle where the grammar requires one.
5. Every sensitive pi refinement `auth_ref` names an actually declared J
   authorization handle `u*`. It never names a node `n*`, instance `i*`, or
   prose authorization kind.
6. C contains only the exact trusted scheduling slots and values from
   `harness_view.json`. It contains no operator, predicate, formula, strategy,
   source/API name, or semantic constant.
7. Pi contains anonymous realization relations only. It contains no dtype,
   shape, operator, formula, predicate, source fragment, frontend API, C value,
   or executable text.
8. Run the supplied static schema validator. Passing it only means the JSON
   envelope is well formed; the external runner still performs canonical
   parsing, dependent TypeCheck, Replay, and Gates in a new phase.

extra.raw_output:
$
  type: "object"
  required: ["schema", "j", "c", "pi"]
  additionalProperties: false
  description: "The response root is one closed object with exactly these fields: schema, j, c, pi. The j object is one closed object with exactly these fields: kernel_id, intent, node_ids, boundary, signature, scopes, storage. Logical callable facts are declared only by j.signature. The root c object is the single implementation-selection object and pi is indexed by j/c. Do not emit interface, harness, location, source, provenance, binding-map or any other root sibling."
  properties: c, j, pi, schema

$.c
  type: "object"
  required: ["slots", "values"]
  additionalProperties: false
  properties: slots, values

$.c.slots
  type: "array"

$.c.slots[]
  type: "object"
  required: ["name", "kind", "role"]
  additionalProperties: false
  properties: kind, name, required, role, value_type

$.c.slots[].kind
  type: "string"
  enum: ["constexpr", "compiler"]

$.c.slots[].name
  type: "string"
  pattern: "^c[0-9]+$"

$.c.slots[].required
  type: "boolean"

$.c.slots[].role
  type: "string"
  pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$"

$.c.slots[].value_type
  type: "string"

$.c.values
  type: "object"
  additionalProperties: {"anyOf": [{"type": "boolean"}, {"type": "integer"}, {"type": "number"}, {"type": "string"}]}

$.j
  type: "object"
  required: ["kernel_id", "intent", "node_ids", "boundary", "signature", "scopes", "storage"]
  additionalProperties: false
  description: "J scopes are an exact derived dominance archive, not a copy of pi regions. Straight-line J uses one parentless function scope. Its definitions are exactly J input handles plus results actually produced by operations in that scope; a declared logical output is not a definition unless an operation really produces that same handle. captures and effects are likewise exact, with no convenience extras. Every semantic loop has exactly one corresponding loop_region scope. The storage array may be empty: ordinary SSA temporaries do not have semantic storage or lifetime objects. Add StorageObject only when J semantics requires storage identity, such as an alias/destination or loop-carried state. write_once requires exactly one matching boundary write event; producing an SSA value is not such an event. Every loop state requires one storage object binding its state, body, next and result values plus a non-literal init value, if any, across iterations."
  properties: boundary, intent, kernel_id, node_ids, scopes, signature, storage

$.j.boundary
  type: "object"
  required: ["domains", "accesses", "broadcasts", "aliases", "effects", "output_mappings", "reductions", "index_bounds", "updates", "result_relations", "realization_authorizations"]
  additionalProperties: false
  description: "The J boundary is one closed object with exactly these fields: domains, accesses, broadcasts, aliases, effects, output_mappings, reductions, index_bounds, updates, result_relations, realization_authorizations. Every load, store, or update access requires a non-empty ordered logical index_expression, including scalar accesses. predicate, fill_value, and logical domains belong only to J when present in source semantics. Preserve every source logical domain, access predicate, and masked-load fill even when the current bound invocation makes a mask tautological. Every access has exactly one EffectSpec whose kind, target, node_ref (including null), and access_ref exactly match that access. Do not move these facts to pi, omit the matching effect, or invent them when the source has none."
  properties: accesses, aliases, broadcasts, domains, effects, index_bounds, output_mappings, realization_authorizations, reductions, result_relations, updates

$.j.boundary.accesses
  type: "array"

$.j.boundary.accesses[]
  type: "object"
  required: ["access_id", "kind", "tensor", "index_expression"]
  additionalProperties: false
  properties: access_id, fill_value, index_expression, kind, node_ref, predicate, tensor

$.j.boundary.accesses[].access_id
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.accesses[].index_expression
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.accesses[].kind
  type: "string"
  enum: ["load", "store", "update"]

$.j.boundary.accesses[].node_ref

$.j.boundary.accesses[].node_ref.anyOf[0]
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.accesses[].node_ref.anyOf[1]
  type: "null"

$.j.boundary.accesses[].predicate

$.j.boundary.accesses[].predicate.anyOf[0]
  type: "string"
  description: "One boolean ContractExpr v1 expression: symbols/literals, arithmetic, comparisons, and/or/not, and only ceil_div/cdiv/min/max calls. No assignment, prose, range notation, frontend calls, attributes, or program/grid/tile/lane coordinate construction."

$.j.boundary.accesses[].predicate.anyOf[1]
  type: "null"

$.j.boundary.accesses[].tensor
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.aliases
  type: "array"

$.j.boundary.aliases[]
  type: "object"
  required: ["left", "right", "kind"]
  additionalProperties: false
  properties: kind, left, right

$.j.boundary.aliases[].kind
  type: "string"
  enum: ["must_alias", "may_alias", "no_alias"]

$.j.boundary.aliases[].left
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.aliases[].right
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.broadcasts
  type: "array"

$.j.boundary.broadcasts[]
  type: "object"
  required: ["node_ref", "operand", "axes"]
  additionalProperties: false
  properties: axes, node_ref, operand

$.j.boundary.broadcasts[].axes
  type: "array"

$.j.boundary.broadcasts[].axes[]

$.j.boundary.broadcasts[].axes[].anyOf[0]
  type: "integer"

$.j.boundary.broadcasts[].axes[].anyOf[1]
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.broadcasts[].operand

  type: "object"
  additionalProperties: {"description": "One boolean ContractExpr v1 expression: symbols/literals, arithmetic, comparisons, and/or/not, and only ceil_div/cdiv/min/max calls. No assignment, prose, range notation, frontend calls, attributes, or program/grid/tile/lane coordinate construction.", "minLength": 1, "type": "string"}
  description: "Map each d* handle directly to one ContractExpr string. Never emit an axes/members/domain object here."

$.j.boundary.effects
  type: "array"

$.j.boundary.effects[]
  type: "object"
  required: ["effect_id", "kind", "target", "access_ref"]
  additionalProperties: false
  properties: access_ref, effect_id, kind, node_ref, target

$.j.boundary.effects[].access_ref

$.j.boundary.effects[].access_ref.anyOf[0]
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.effects[].access_ref.anyOf[1]
  type: "null"

$.j.boundary.effects[].effect_id
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.effects[].kind
  type: "string"
  enum: ["read", "write", "read_write", "update"]

$.j.boundary.effects[].node_ref

$.j.boundary.effects[].node_ref.anyOf[0]
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.effects[].node_ref.anyOf[1]
  type: "null"

$.j.boundary.effects[].target
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.index_bounds
  type: "array"

$.j.boundary.index_bounds[]
  type: "object"
  required: ["node_ref", "data", "indices", "axis"]
  additionalProperties: false
  description: "Typed precondition 0 <= indices < dim(data, axis), exactly bound to one gather/scatter node. Never use a proof string or proven flag."
  properties: axis, data, indices, node_ref

$.j.boundary.index_bounds[].axis
  type: "integer"
  minimum: 0

$.j.boundary.index_bounds[].data
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.index_bounds[].indices
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.index_bounds[].node_ref
  type: "string"

$.j.boundary.output_mappings

  description: "Pi has exactly two reference roles. instances[k].semantic_ref is an anchor into a declared anonymous J/C handle; J.signature handles are ordinary J handles and there is no interface namespace. It is not a pi graph node. instances[k].id declares the only pi graph-node namespace i0,i1,... in declaration order. Every routes source/target, order before/after, and sharing source/consumer must equal one already declared instance id i*. Edges never use raw t*/n*/a*/d*/e*/q*/b*/s*/v*/p*/c*/x* handles and never declare instances implicitly. To represent a p0 dependency on access a0, declare i0 anchored by p0 and i1 anchored by a0, then route i0 to i1; routing p0 to i1 is invalid. Multiple instances may share one semantic_ref when the source has multiple compiler-visible stages. Route slots are distinct, non-negative, target-local opaque input ordinals. Pi mechanism is one closed source-neutral event class. realize is a generic representation-only stage when no more specific class applies. One realize instance anchored directly to a J.signature handle or C slot may be discharged by that parameter binding and its direct routed use; it does not require an identity assignment. Multiple instances anchored to the same handle still denote distinct routed use-sites/stages. address_base is an independently compiler-visible, program-uniform pointer/base stage before lane broadcast or lane-varying addressing; Lift uses it only when that separate source stage exists. address_lane is the compiler-visible stage that forms lane-varying final addresses. When routes contain address_base -> address_lane, Replay must materialize two distinct stages in that order and must not algebraically fold them into one flat vector offset. transfer_direct and transfer_async classify data movement after address formation; update_atomic and update_privatized classify physical update realization; synchronize classifies synchronization. Region placement='program' only scopes an instance to one program; it does not assert that a program/grid coordinate is read. A compiler-visible program/grid coordinate is a separate realization stage and requires its own realize instance and routes. Its source-neutral encoding is a realize instance anchored to the corresponding J domain in a program region whose scalar dependency path enters address_base before transfer; a domain/C dependency path entering address_lane is lane-varying instead. Replay must preserve this base-versus-lane distinction and U_f maps it to public frontend APIs. Integer coordinate arithmetic is a realize stage, not address_base or address_lane merely because the resulting integer is later used as a pointer offset. If source forms one complete base-plus-lane integer coordinate and then performs one pointer addition, Lift records that single pointer operation as address_lane; it must not invent an extra pointer address_base for the coordinate's program-uniform component. Replay must not invent program_id, a grid offset, or an affine address stage from region placement, grid convention, or C alone. Address classes never carry an index/offset formula, constant, integer width, cast, dtype, shape, vector length, predicate, fill, frontend API, or logical access semantics.   description: "Pi mechanism is one closed source-neutral event class. realize is a generic representation-only stage when no more specific class applies. One realize instance anchored directly to a J.signature handle or C slot may be discharged by that parameter binding and its direct routed use; it does not require an identity assignment. Multiple instances anchored to the same handle still denote distinct routed use-sites/stages. address_base is an independently compiler-visible, program-uniform pointer/base stage before lane broadcast or lane-varying addressing; Lift uses it only when that separate source stage exists. address_lane is the compiler-visible stage that forms lane-varying final addresses. When routes contain address_base -> address_lane, Replay must materialize two distinct stages in that order and must not algebraically fold them into one flat vector offset. transfer_direct and transfer_async classify data movement after address formation; update_atomic and update_privatized classify physical update realization; synchronize classifies synchronization. Region placement='program' only scopes an instance to one program; it does not assert that a program/grid coordinate is read. A compiler-visible program/grid coordinate is a separate realization stage and requires its own realize instance and routes. Its source-neutral encoding is a realize instance anchored to the corresponding J domain in a program region whose scalar dependency path enters address_base before transfer; a domain/C dependency path entering address_lane is lane-varying instead. Replay must preserve this base-versus-lane distinction and U_f maps it to public frontend APIs. Integer coordinate arithmetic is a realize stage, not address_base or address_lane merely because the resulting integer is later used as a pointer offset. If source forms one complete base-plus-lane integer coordinate and then performs one pointer addition, Lift records that single pointer operation as address_lane; it must not invent an extra pointer address_base for the coordinate's program-uniform component. Replay must not invent program_id, a grid offset, or an affine address stage from region placement, grid convention, or C alone. Address classes never carry an index/offset formula, constant, integer width, cast, dtype, shape, vector length, predicate, fill, frontend API, or logical access semantics."
